title: American Airlines 1
summary: American Airlines Flight 1 departed from Memphis Municipal Airport at 7:04 p.m. bound for Little Rock. The last contact with the flight crew was at 7:18 p.m. as the aircraft was heading towards Little Rock. The aircraft later crashed into a swamp near Goodwin, Arkansas, disintegrating on impact and killing all 17 people on board.
probable_cause: The board ruled out the possibility of a purely mechanical failure but could not determine the probable cause. Contributing factors may have included flying at a low altitude, possible interference with the pilots' sight by a passenger in the cockpit, switching of an empty gas tank for a full one, and confusion on the part of the first officer.

factors.evidence: interference with the pilots' sight by a passenger in the cockpit
switching of an empty gas tank for a full one that may have caused a sudden drop into the tree line
aircraft crashed into a swamp near Goodwin, Arkansas, disintegrating on impact

events.text: The aircraft departed from Memphis Municipal Airport on January 14, 1936 at 7:04 p.m.
The last contact with the flight crew was at 7:18 p.m. as the aircraft was heading towards Little Rock.
The aircraft crashed into a swamp near Goodwin, Arkansas, about 2 mi north of U.S. Highway 70, disintegrating on impact.

notes: Probable cause could not be determined by investigation
Multiple conflicting theories but none confirmed

title: Chicago and Southern 4
summary: A Lockheed Electra crashed in a farm field near the Missouri River five minutes after departing St. Louis at 9:52 PM, killing all eight occupants. Witnesses reported hearing aircraft engines roaring wide open and then stopping, observing the plane flying low and banking sharply to the left as though attempting to return to the airport. The aircraft struck and cut a triangular swath across a cornfield before turning over.
probable_cause: Unknown. The text does not provide an official investigation conclusion or probable cause statement.

factors.evidence: the motors of the plane roaring wide open and then the motors stopped
the plane flying low and bank sharply to the left
cut a triangular swath across a cornfield before it turned over
the pilot, encountering bad visibility, had decided to return to the airport

events.text: The aircraft departed St. Louis at 9:52 PM, and was scheduled to arrive in Chicago at 12:55 AM.
Five minutes after departure, all radio contact was lost with the aircraft.
The wrist watch of the dead pilot stopped at 10:02, indicating the time of the crash was around 10 minutes after departure.
With the pilot apparently attempting to nose up, the heavy 10-passenger Lockheed-Electra cut a triangular swath across a cornfield before it turned over.

notes: no official investigation report available in text

title: 1936 KLM Croydon accident
summary: The Douglas DC-2 took off from Croydon Airport in dense fog with visibility of approximately 50 meters under instrument flight rules conditions. Crews followed a white line on the grass surface for takeoff guidance. The KLM aircraft veered off the white line after about 200 yards and, after becoming airborne, headed south toward rising ground instead of the normal westerly direction. The aircraft struck a house chimney and crashed, killing 15 of 17 occupants.
probable_cause: Aircraft veered off the white line takeoff path and adopted incorrect heading toward rising ground after becoming airborne in severe fog, resulting in controlled flight into terrain.

factors.evidence: Croydon Air Port was shrouded in fog with visibility fluctuating at around 50 m.
Aircraft veered off line to the left after about 200 yd and on becoming airborne headed south towards rising ground instead of normal westerly direction.
White line laid out on grass surface during takeoff used at time; crews following white line at Croydon since 1931.
Aircraft hit chimney of house on Hillcrest Road and crashed into empty house opposite side of street.

events.text: Douglas DC-2 begins takeoff from Croydon Airport in fog with visibility 50 meters, following white line on grass.
Aircraft veers to the left off white line after approximately 200 yards during takeoff run.
Aircraft becomes airborne and heads south toward rising ground instead of normal westerly direction.
Aircraft hit chimney of house on Hillcrest Road and crashed into house; one survivor died at Purley Hospital.

notes: Investigation terminated on 16 December without reaching verdict
White line takeoff procedure standard at Croydon at time
Prior incident: Air France aircraft crashed same procedure May 1934

title: United Airlines Trip 34
summary: United Air Lines Flight 34 departed Mills Field in San Francisco on December 27, 1936 bound for Los Angeles. At 7:36 am Pacific time, the co-pilot requested the UAL localizer beacon at Burbank be turned on. Two minutes later at 7:38 am, the aircraft crashed at the head of Rice Canyon near Newhall, killing all 12 passengers and crew. The probable cause was determined to be the pilot's error in attempting to fly through Newhall pass at an altitude lower than the surrounding mountains without first determining the weather by radio.
probable_cause: An error on the part of the pilot for attempting to fly through Newhall pass at an altitude lower than the surrounding mountains without first determining by radio the existing weather.
